data.name: Pranshul
data.gender_notes: Pranshul is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Pranshul is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Prasnshu' which means 'the grace of Lord Shiva'. This name is believed to bring blessings of Lord Shiva and is often given to boys as a sign of his divine grace and protection. The name Pranshul carries the meaning “Lord Shiva's grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pranshul usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of Lord Shiva's blessings and protection
data.etymology: Pranshul belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Shiva's grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pranshul total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference:
Pranshul was a famous Hindu king of the Chalukya dynasty in the late 10th century.
He ruled from his capital Vatapi, which is now known as Badami in Karnataka.
Pranshul was a great patron of art and architecture.
He is famous for building several temples in the Dravidian style.
He defeated several rulers and expanded his kingdom during his reign.
historical_references.context: Hindu King of the Chalukya Dynasty, Patron of Art and Architecture, Expanded his Kingdom, Built Several Temples in the Dravidian Style, Defeated Several Rulers

historical_references.reference:
Pranshul was a Hindu warrior and commander in the army of the Mughal Emperor Akbar.
He is best known for his bravery in the Battle of Haldighati fought in 1576 between Akbar and Maharana Pratap of Mewar.
Pranshul led the left wing of the Mughal army and played a crucial role in the battle.
He was later rewarded with the title Raja Mansingh and was made the governor of Amber.
historical_references.context: Hindu Warrior and Commander in the Army of Mughal Emperor Akbar, Famous for Bravery in Battle of Haldighati, Led Left Wing of Mughal Army, Later Rewarded with Title Raja Mansingh and Made Governor of Amber
